channel.title: Hesed Words — Reflections
channel.description: Devotional reflections by Norm Reed. Scripture, justice, and the love that holds. Written for the road.

item.title: The Piece I Keep Picking Up
item.description: Reading to the end of Zechariah and not finishing it. The book had every reason to end on the throne, or at the open door in the mountain. It ends in a kitchen, with someone reaching for a pot.

item.title: The One Thing He Wouldn't Delegate
item.description: A young man in Zechariah's second vision is stopped mid-survey — the cord was not the wrong instrument, just not the last word. A hard man in Papua New Guinea handed over every authority except the one to be merciful.

item.title: The Vow?
item.description: Psalm 61 asks four times for a place, and every shelter in it has an owner. Then a vow appears and the prayer tilts: heard first, performed last, with the shelter sitting in between. Not the shape of a bargain.

item.title: What Is Wicked in This Story?
item.description: Psalm 58 ends with the righteous bathing their feet in the blood of the wicked — unusable, until verse one turns out to say who it's actually addressed to. Not criminals. The bench.

item.title: Those Who Know Their God
item.description: Daniel 11:32 promises the people who know their God shall be strong and do exploits — a verse that once became, for a young Christian with an explanation for every date, a chapter about knowing better instead of knowing God.

item.title: This I Know
item.description: Psalm 56 never says we, only I. Batach — to lean your whole weight on something and find out whether it holds. This I know, that God is for me — a line that only comes after the tossings have been numbered.

item.title: Pride
item.description: Waking with thoughts upon the bed, like Nebuchadnezzar in Daniel 4 — and the discovery that pride never feels like pride from the inside, only ever like accuracy. The verdict we reach about our own humility is useless.

item.title: I Am Like an Olive Tree
item.description: Two men stand in the same psalm under the same verb. Doeg trusted in the abundance of his riches; David answers, but I am like a green olive tree in the house of God. Batach — the same posture, different ground.

item.title: Coincidence
item.description: The book of Esther never once names God, and reads at first like a story about luck — until nahafokh hu, it was turned about, arrives at the pivot. A reflection on the dice that named Purim, and a Friday-the-thirteenth morning that turned the same way.

item.title: The Sacrifice of Thanksgiving
item.description: Psalm 50 opens like a courtroom, and the first thing God says is that he is not hungry — the offerings were never supply. What he wants: offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving; the one who offers thanksgiving glorifies me.

item.title: Understanding?
item.description: Reading Psalm 49, a state funeral came back to me. 'Man in his pomp, yet without understanding, is like the beasts that perish.' Not intelligence. Da'at — the knowing of God that is not in the head but in the hands.

item.title: In the Midst of the Temple
item.description: Psalm 48 builds the city — and then Selah. When the pause ends, the question surfaces: not what does the city look like, but what is it for? If hesed is what Zion is built on, does my life exude it? Does the church?

item.title: See Me Trying
item.description: I had misread Nehemiah's prayer as ledger-keeping. It is the vulnerability of worship itself: a child carrying a crayon drawing to their father. Not asking for payment. Asking to be seen.

item.title: Is There Not a Cause
item.description: I wanted a cause to die for. The King rides for truth, meekness, and righteousness — not toward them but on account of them. They are not the objective; they are what the ride is made of.

item.title: Not the Lesson I First Thought
item.description: In Ezra 4 the neighbours offer to help build, and Zerubbabel refuses. They raised worship; he answered architecture. They thought they were building a house. They were meant to be gathering worshippers.

item.title: Our God-Sponsored Projects
item.description: Ezra–Nehemiah records what men finished and could not keep. Jesus is building what he has not finished — and therefore cannot lose.

item.title: A Place for Salt
item.description: Ezekiel's river heals the Dead Sea — and then one line no one preaches: 'but its swamps and marshes will not become fresh; they are to be left for salt.' In the greatest picture of renewal in the prophets, the salt stays.
